the_line: Lean proves that a conclusion follows from stated premises. It does not adjudicate reality. Every theorem in this repo is of the form 'if these premises hold, then this follows', and a kernel proof of it is silent on whether any organism satisfies the premises. So a grand question has a formalisable core exactly to the extent that part of the disagreement about it is a disagreement about what follows from what, and an empirical remainder exactly to the extent that it is a disagreement about what the world is like. Most of these questions are mostly remainder. Two of them (the Price equation, Hamilton's rule) are disputes in which the formal part has been repeatedly confused with the empirical part for decades, and those are the ones where formalisation would do the most good. A capability map that let the first kind of progress be read as the second would be worse than no map.
name: Evolvability
question: What makes a lineage able to generate useful variation, and is that capacity itself a product of selection?

statements.claim: If a genotype space is given with a stated mutational neighbourhood relation, then the set of phenotypes reachable within k mutations from a stated genotype is determined, so a claim that a phenotype is reachable in fewer is impossible.
statements.settles: Reachability and distance claims in a stated genotype space. This repo's codon-space distance is the one-step instance of exactly this, decided by the kernel over a finite table, so the generalisation has a working precedent here.

statements.claim: If two systems have stated mutational neighbourhoods and a stated phenotype-accessibility measure, then one is more evolvable than the other under that measure, or the comparison does not follow.
statements.settles: That 'more evolvable' is a claim relative to a stated measure, and which comparisons are consequences of the stated structures. It does not settle which measure of evolvability is the biologically relevant one.

statements.claim: If a pleiotropy graph is stated, then a claimed modular decomposition of it either follows or does not.
statements.settles: The modularity half of the modularity-evolvability link, as a graph-structural question. The closure machinery for views of such a graph is proved here.

items.what: Whether real genotype spaces have the stated neighbourhood structure.
items.measurement: Deep mutational scanning with phenotype assayed for every variant in a defined neighbourhood.

items.what: Whether evolvability is itself under selection, or a by-product of selection for something else.
items.why_not_provable: A causal claim about history. Pigliucci's question, and it is empirical.
items.measurement: Experimental evolution with variability-generating mechanisms as the measured trait, over many lineages.

items.what: Which of the many proposed measures of evolvability predicts anything.
items.measurement: Prospective tests: measure the candidate quantity, then observe which lineages adapt.

items.what: The relationship between robustness and evolvability, which is enumerated as an open problem in its own right here.
items.why_not_provable: Both can be defined formally; whether they trade off in real systems is a fact about those systems.
items.measurement: Paired measurement of mutational robustness and adaptive rate in the same systems.

in_repo.ref: Delphi.Genotype.minSubst and the decided codon distances
in_repo.note: Graph distance in a finite genotype space, decided rather than asserted. The generalisation to an arbitrary stated neighbourhood is the missing module and would reuse this idiom directly.
Closure of a view under a stated relation, and acyclicity of a stated developmental ordering, both proved from Boolean checks.
Four distinct evolvability problems enumerated with sources, including the robustness-evolvability relation and the pleiotropy-modularity-evolvability relation.

A conditional flow-matching or DDPM model over 16,123 real body shapes generates candidate organisms. It samples a learned distribution; it does not explore a stated mutational neighbourhood, so it is not an evolvability tool.

tools_needed.name: lean_module_genotype_network
tools_needed.note: Reachability and distance in a stated genotype space, generalising the proved codon-space case. This single module serves evolvability, the genotype-phenotype map and predicting evolution.

tools_needed.name: open_questions_list
tools_needed.note: The literature enumeration in open-problems/ is reachable from no tool. The open-questions thread's lean_open_questions serves a different thing: this project's own seven open questions with Lean-formalised arms, not the field's.

tools_needed.name: omics_search
tools_needed.note: Finds genes by pathway and anatomy term, which is where a pleiotropy graph for a real organism would be assembled from.

wagner1996.ref: Wagner GP, Altenberg L (1996). Perspective: Complex adaptations and the evolution of evolvability. Evolution 50:967-976.
wagner1996.quotable: The problem of complex adaptations is studied in two largely disconnected research traditions: evolutionary biology and evolutionary computer science
wagner1996.note: FOUNDATIONAL. The Europe PMC title is in capitals in the record.

pigliucci2008.ref: Pigliucci M (2008). Is evolvability evolvable? Nature Reviews Genetics 9:75-82.
pigliucci2008.quotable: biologists have increasingly been asking whether the ability to evolve--the evolvability--of biological systems, itself evolves

payne2019.ref: Payne JL, Wagner A (2019). The causes of evolvability and their evolution. Nature Reviews Genetics 20:24-38.
payne2019.quotable: Evolvability is the ability of a biological system to produce phenotypic variation that is both heritable and adaptive

wagner2011pleiotropy.ref: Wagner GP, Zhang J (2011). The pleiotropic structure of the genotype-phenotype map: the evolvability of complex organisms. Nature Reviews Genetics 12:204-213.
wagner2011pleiotropy.quotable: Because pleiotropy was found so frequently, the notion arose that pleiotropy is 'universal'
wagner2011pleiotropy.note: structural account of why the genotype-phenotype map is hard

scope: This is a map of what is formalisable, not a research programme and not a claim that the formalisable parts are the important parts. The (a)/(b) split is a judgement made here and is arguable for every entry; where it is contentious the dispute field says so. The list is not exhaust: there is no canonical set of grand questions in biology, and this one is weighted toward evolution, development and scaling because that is what this project reads. Several entries have no counterpart in open-problems/problems.json, which is a gap in that enumeration rather than evidence the question is settled. Nothing here is about the held-out exam clade.
